title: Managing Hotel Stays & Accommodation Requests
titleEs: Gestionar la estancia en el hotel y las peticiones de alojamiento
summary: Haz peticiones y reclamaciones en el hotel: *Would it be possible to…?*, promesas con *will* y condiciones con el First Conditional.
canDo: Puedo hacer peticiones muy corteses con *Would it be possible to…?*.
Puedo entender promesas y ofrecimientos del personal (*I'll send someone up*).
Puedo entender y negociar condiciones (*If you need the room until two, there will be a charge*).
Puedo pronunciar *luggage* con /dʒ/ final, *suite* como *sweet* y *stairs* sin /e/ inicial.

focus.grammar: will para prometer y ofrecer · Would it be possible to + verbo base? · If + presente, there will be… · Present Continuous para planes (We're checking out on Monday)
focus.lexis: check in / check out, a late check-out, Is breakfast included?, extra towels, straight away, send someone up, a different room, luggage, Should you require…
focus.afh: s-cluster st- (stairs) · /dʒ/ final en luggage · suite = /swiːt/ · s = /z/ en reservation · diptongo /aʊ/ en towels

warmup: Piensa en la última vez que algo falló en un hotel o en un alojamiento: la calefacción, el ruido, la limpieza… ¿Cómo lo pediste o lo reclamaste?

scenario.title: Respuesta del hotel
scenario.context: Por la huelga de trenes (Lección 27), Priya avisó al hotel de Edimburgo de que llegarían muy tarde y pidió una habitación tranquila. Sophie, la recepcionista, le responde.
scenario.speaker: sophie
scenario.text: Dear Priya, thank you for your message, and I'm sorry to hear about the strike. Please don't worry about your late arrival: our reception is open twenty-four hours, so someone {{will be}} here when you arrive. {{I'll make sure}} your room is on a high floor, away from the street. {{If you need}} a taxi from the station, {{we'll be happy to}} book one for you. We look forward to welcoming you. Kind regards, Sophie Bennett, Reception

discovery.intro: Sophie promete soluciones y explica una condición. Fíjate en el verbo que usa para prometer y en cómo se forma el futuro de *there is*.
discovery.speaker: ryan
discovery.text: {{I'll send}} someone up straight away. {{If you need}} the room until two, {{there will be}} a small charge.

questions.q: ¿Qué hace la recepcionista con *I'll send someone up*?
questions.explain: *Will* sirve para prometer y ofrecer: el personal se compromete a actuar.

questions.q: ¿Qué forma tiene el futuro de *there is / there are*?
questions.explain: *There will be a small charge* = habrá un pequeño recargo.

questions.q: Quieres pedir una habitación más tranquila. ¿Qué frase es más adecuada en un hotel?
options: Would it be possible to have a quieter room?
questions.explain: *Would it be possible to…?* es la petición más cortés. Las otras suenan bruscas, y *other room* es incorrecto.

points: *Will* para prometer y ofrecer, típico del personal: *I'll send someone up.*
Present Continuous para planes cerrados (Lección 26): *We're checking out on Monday.*
First Conditional para las condiciones: *If you need the room until two, there will be a charge.*
*Would it be possible to* + verbo base: la petición más cortés.
formulas: Would it be possible to + verbo base?
If + presente, there will be + sustantivo
rule.note: «Otra habitación» es *a different room* (distinta) o *another room* (una más), nunca *other room*. Y *luggage* es incontable: *my luggage*, no *my luggages*.

phonetics.intro: En el hotel aparecen palabras con trampas para el hispanohablante: *suite* no se pronuncia como se escribe, *luggage* termina en /dʒ/, *stairs* lleva el grupo st- y *reservation* tiene una s que suena /z/.

alerts.text: Acento en la primera sílaba, LUG.
La u es /ʌ/: una a corta, «LÁ».

example.speaker: sophie
example.text: We can keep your luggage after check-out.

alerts.text: La v es /v/, con el labio inferior bajo los dientes.
Acento principal en VA, la tercera sílaba.

example.speaker: priya
example.text: I have a reservation for three nights.

alerts.text: Se pronuncia igual que *sweet*: «suiit». No digas «suit».
*Su-* es /sw/: la s y una u rápida, juntas.

example.speaker: sophie
example.text: We can upgrade you to a suite tonight.

alerts.text: En EE. UU. suena «er»; en Reino Unido, «ea», sin r.

example.speaker: sophie
example.text: The lift is out of order, so please use the stairs.

alerts.text: La segunda sílaba es una schwa muy corta: «TÁU-lz».

task.title: Escribe al hotel antes de llegar
task.scenario: Tienes una reserva de hotel para un viaje. Vas a llegar tarde y necesitas pedir algunas cosas. Escribe al hotel antes de tu llegada.
task.brief: Write to a hotel before your stay to explain your plans and make some requests.
steps: Di que tienes una reserva y para qué fechas (*I have a reservation for…*).
Explica tus planes con el Present Continuous (*We're arriving late…*).
Haz dos peticiones corteses (*Would it be possible to…? / Could we…?*).
Acepta una posible condición con el First Conditional (*If there is an extra charge, that will be fine*) y despídete.
frames: Dear Sir or Madam, I have a reservation for ___ from ___ to ___.
Unfortunately, we're arriving at ___. Will someone be at reception?
If there is an extra charge, that will be fine.
Could we ___ after check-out? Many thanks, ___

extra.title: Extra: el aviso del hotel
extra.brief: Write a formal hotel notice about late check-out.
frames: Should you require a late check-out, please inform reception by ___. There will be a charge of ___ for departures after ___.

parts.speaker: sarah
parts.text: Dear Sir or Madam, I have a {{reservation}} for two people from April 18 to April 21. Unfortunately, our train is delayed, so we{{'re arriving}} at around eleven at night. Will someone be at reception? Also, {{would it be possible to}} have a quiet room on a high floor? {{If there is}} an extra charge, {{that will be}} fine. Finally, we{{'re leaving}} for the airport at three on Monday. {{Could we}} leave our luggage at the hotel after check-out? Many thanks, Sarah
parts.tts: Dear Sir or Madam, I have a reservation for two people from April eighteenth to April twenty-first. Unfortunately, our train is delayed, so we're arriving at around eleven at night. Will someone be at reception? Also, would it be possible to have a quiet room on a high floor? If there is an extra charge, that will be fine. Finally, we're leaving for the airport at three on Monday. Could we leave our luggage at the hotel after check-out? Many thanks, Sarah
parts.label: Correo al hotel (neutro)
notes: *We're arriving*, *we're leaving*: planes cerrados con el Present Continuous.
*Would it be possible to…?* y *Could we…?*: peticiones corteses. *If there is…, that will be fine*: aceptar una condición.

parts.speaker: sophie
parts.text: {{Should you require}} a late check-out, please inform reception by ten o'clock. {{There will be}} a charge of twenty pounds for departures after midday.
parts.label: Aviso del hotel (formal)
notes: *Should you require* = *If you need* en registro muy formal.
*There will be a charge…*: condición expresada con el futuro de *there is*.
